concerns.text: Circularity / Constitution VI violation: FR-001 derives `authenticity_score` from the user's own comment corpus (vulnerability markers like 'I'm struggling') and FR-002 derives `self_eval_score` from the SAME corpus (sentiment + self-reference). Predictor and outcome are summaries of the same text stream — a user who writes vulnerable, negative-sentiment, first-person text will score high on both by construction. The moderation of self-evaluation by 'authenticity' is then partly an artifact of shared lexical signal (first-person pronouns and negative sentiment drive both scores). The spec must separate streams: authenticity/engagement features should characterize the content a user is EXPOSED to (others' posts), not the user's own comments.

`exposure_level` — the primary predictor in the moderation model — is never defined or extracted. No FR specifies how exposure to idealized self-presentation is measured (which subreddits, what counts as exposure, over what window). US-2 scenario 1 references a dataset 'with exposure_level' but no upstream FR produces it. Without an operational definition, the core moderation analysis cannot be executed or validated.

'Then the output includes a statistically significant interaction term coefficient (if present) with a p-value < 0.05' — acceptance criteria must not presuppose a significant finding; significance is an empirical outcome, not a system requirement. This conflates pipeline correctness with the research result and biases toward false-positive reporting.

Demographic stratification via keyword matching in user text ('19M', 'female') is acknowledged as noisy, but the spec does not address the selection bias this induces (only users who self-disclose demographics are stratified) or require reporting subgroup N and proxy-coverage rates. With noisy, non-random subgroup assignment, between-subgroup coefficient differences are uninterpretable without at least a coverage/attrition report per subgroup.

SC-006's sensitivity sweep (±0.05 on 'self-reference or sentiment thresholds') is described but the thresholds themselves are never defined in any FR; the criterion references parameters the spec does not specify.
